hook.line: When you write about causes, you need a verb for "this started that" that is not just *causar*. *Dar lugar a* is the quiet, serious one you will see in every newspaper.
hook.es: La crisis dio lugar a una ola de protestas.
hook.en: The crisis gave rise to a wave of protests.

examples.es: La crisis dio lugar a una ola de protestas.
examples.en: The crisis gave rise to a wave of protests.

examples.es: Esto puede dar lugar a malentendidos.
La venta del edificio dio lugar a una protesta.
examples.en: The sale of the building gave rise to a protest.

examples.es: Esa pregunta dio lugar a un largo debate.
examples.en: That question gave rise to a long debate.
What gave rise to this fight?

examples.es: No quiero dar lugar a dudas.
examples.en: I don't want to leave room for doubt.

rule:
*Dar lugar a* means to give rise to, or to lead to. The cause is the subject and the result comes after *a*: *la crisis dio lugar a una ola de protestas*.

Only *dar* changes: *dio lugar*, *dieron lugar*, *puede dar lugar*.

After *a* usually comes a noun: *dio lugar a protestas*. A whole clause is possible too (*dio lugar a que la gente protestara*), but in an essay the noun is shorter and cleaner. With *el*, *a* joins it: *dio lugar al conflicto*.
smallPrint: Teachers call this a support-verb phrase: *dar* carries little meaning on its own, and the noun *lugar* does the work.

readAndPick.es: La crisis dio lugar a una ola de protestas.
options: The crisis gave rise to a wave of protests.
The crisis put an end to a wave of protests.
The crisis took the place of a wave of protests.

readAndPick.es: Esto puede dar lugar a malentendidos.
options: This was a misunderstanding.
This can lead to misunderstandings.
This avoids misunderstandings.

readAndPick.es: Las dudas dieron lugar a un divorcio.
options: The doubt gave rise to a divorce.
The doubts gave rise to a divorce.
The doubts gave rise to some divorces.

readAndPick.es: El error dio lugar a la crisis.
options: The error gave rise to the crisis.
The errors gave rise to the crisis.
The error will give rise to the crisis.
What will give rise to this fight?
What gave rise to this fight?
What gives rise to this fight?

readAndPick.es: Esa idea no dará lugar a nada bueno.
options: That idea didn't lead to anything good.
That idea doesn't lead to anything good.
That idea won't lead to anything good.

readAndPick.es: Los cambios dieron lugar a un nuevo barrio.
options: The changes gave rise to a new neighbourhood.
The change gave rise to a new neighbourhood.
The changes will give rise to a new neighbourhood.

readAndPick.es: Una palabra mal dicha puede dar lugar a un problema.
options: A badly said word led to a problem.
A badly said word can lead to a problem.
A badly said word is a problem.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *La crisis dio ___ a una ola de protestas.* (*lugar* or *sitio*) The crisis gave rise to a wave of protests.
yourTurn.answer: La crisis dio lugar a una ola de protestas.
yourTurn.why: The fixed phrase is *dar lugar a*.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick and type the whole sentence: *Esa pregunta ___ lugar a un largo debate.* (*dio* or *dieron*) That question gave rise to a long debate.
yourTurn.answer: Esa pregunta dio lugar a un largo debate.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: This can lead to misunderstandings.
yourTurn.answer: Esto puede dar lugar a malentendidos.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: What gave rise to this fight?
yourTurn.why: *Qué* is the cause, so it is the subject of *dio*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: The error gave rise to the crisis.
yourTurn.answer: El error dio lugar a la crisis.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it plural: *El cambio dio lugar a un conflicto.* (use *los cambios*)
yourTurn.answer: Los cambios dieron lugar a un conflicto.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about the future: *La venta dio lugar a una protesta.*
yourTurn.answer: La venta dará lugar a una protesta.
accept: La venta va a dar lugar a una protesta.

pitfalls.wrong: La protesta dio lugar en la plaza.
pitfalls.right: La protesta tuvo lugar en la plaza.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *Dar lugar a* is "give rise to"; for "take place", Spanish says *tener lugar*.

pitfalls.right: La crisis dio lugar a protestas.
pitfalls.why: Almost. English says "gave rise" with no little word, but Spanish needs the *a*.

pitfalls.wrong: La crisis dio un lugar a una ola de protestas.
pitfalls.right: La crisis dio lugar a una ola de protestas.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The phrase is fixed: *dar lugar*, with no *un* in between.

personal: Think of something that started a chain of events in your life or city. Say it: *… dio lugar a…*.
